```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "95%"
)

report_file <- normalizePath(
  knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
study_root <- normalizePath(
  file.path(dirname(report_file), ".."), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
project_root <- normalizePath(
  file.path(study_root, ".."), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
figure4_dir <- file.path(study_root, "results", "figure4")
figure6_dir <- file.path(study_root, "results", "figure6")

required_files <- c(
  file.path(figure4_dir, "figure4_raw.csv"),
  file.path(figure4_dir, "figure4_summary.csv"),
  file.path(figure4_dir, "figure4_cv_bias.png"),
  file.path(figure6_dir, "figure6_raw.csv"),
  file.path(figure6_dir, "figure6_summary.csv"),
  file.path(figure6_dir, "figure6_pse_comparison.png")
)

if (!all(file.exists(required_files))) {
  stop(
    "Simulation outputs are incomplete. Run the Figure 4 and Figure 6 ",
    "scripts in simulation_study/scripts before knitting this document."
  )
}

figure4_raw <- read.csv(file.path(figure4_dir, "figure4_raw.csv"))
figure4_summary <- read.csv(file.path(figure4_dir, "figure4_summary.csv"))
figure6_raw <- read.csv(file.path(figure6_dir, "figure6_raw.csv"))

figure6_alpha <- read.csv(file.path(figure6_dir, "figure6_alpha_selection.csv"))
```

# Purpose

This document records two preliminary simulation experiments based on Figures 4
and 6 in Craig et al. (2025), *Pretraining and the lasso*. The simulations retain
the data-generating structures, model comparisons, and primary performance
measures stated in the article. Reproducibility additions include fixed random
seeds, checkpointed Monte Carlo results, explicit software versions, and saved
raw results for every replication.

# Figure 4: cross-validation error

## Design

The simulation has nine groups with 55 observations per group, giving
\(n=495\), and \(p=1000\) independent standard-normal predictors. The first ten
coefficients are common to every group and equal 2.5. Each group has ten
additional nonzero coefficients equal to 2.5 on a group-specific, nonoverlapping
block of variables. Gaussian errors have standard deviation 10. An independent
test set contains 4,950 observations.

The fitted models are Overall Lasso, Pretrained Lasso at
\(\alpha\in\{0,0.5,0.95\}\), and Individual Lasso. We compare three-fold and
ten-fold cross-validation and the `lambda.1se` and `lambda.min` rules. Following
Figure 4, the reported quantity is

\[
100\frac{\mathrm{test\ error}-\mathrm{CV\ error}}
         {\mathrm{test\ error}}.
\]

```{r figure4-counts, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
  "The current output contains **%d complete Monte Carlo replications** and %d model-setting observations.\n\n",
  length(unique(figure4_raw$replication)), nrow(figure4_raw)
))
```

## Results

```{r figure4-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Cross-validation bias experiment corresponding to Figure 4."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure4_dir, "figure4_cv_bias.png"))
```

```{r figure4-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
figure4_display <- figure4_summary[, c(
  "nfolds", "lambda_rule", "model", "mean_relative_bias",
  "median_relative_bias", "q025_relative_bias", "q975_relative_bias"
)]
names(figure4_display) <- c(
  "Folds", "Lambda rule", "Model", "Mean bias (%)", "Median bias (%)",
  "2.5%", "97.5%"
)
numeric_columns <- vapply(figure4_display, is.numeric, logical(1))
numeric_columns[1L] <- FALSE
figure4_display[numeric_columns] <- lapply(
  figure4_display[numeric_columns], round, digits = 2
)
print(knitr::kable(figure4_display, booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE))
```

With three folds and `lambda.1se`, the absolute mean relative bias is no more
than 4.63% for any of the five models. With ten folds and `lambda.min`, the
mean optimistic bias reaches 11.09% for \(\alpha=0\) and 15.46% for
\(\alpha=0.5\). The observed simulation pattern therefore supports the article's
recommendation to use conservative first-stage regularization and a small
number of folds.

The conventional signal-to-noise ratio calculated as
\(\operatorname{Var}(X\beta)/\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon)\) is approximately
`r round(mean(figure4_raw$empirical_snr), 2)` in our generated samples. The
explicit coefficient and noise settings in the article imply a theoretical
value of `r unique(figure4_raw$theoretical_snr)[1]` under this definition. This
quantity is saved because the Figure 4 caption reports a mean SNR of 1.8 while
the stated coefficients and noise standard deviation imply a different value
under the conventional variance ratio.

# Figure 6: external pretraining data

## Design

The external dataset \(D_1\) contains ten groups, 100 observations per group,
and 500 predictors. Dataset \(D_2\) contains 100 additional observations from
the distribution of group 1, and the independent group-1 test set also contains
100 observations. Coefficients are generated from

\[
\beta_g=\rho\beta_{\mathrm{shared}}+
(1-\rho)\beta_{g,\mathrm{individual}},
\qquad \rho\in\{0,0.5,1\}.
\]

The shared component and every group-specific component have ten nonzero
entries. Group-specific supports do not overlap. Gaussian noise is scaled to a
target average SNR of 1.8. We compare: Lasso on \(D_2\) only; Pretrained Lasso
using \(D_1\) followed by \(D_2\); Lasso using group 1 from \(D_1\) combined
with \(D_2\); and Lasso using all of \(D_1\) combined with \(D_2\).

```{r figure6-counts, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
  "The current output contains **%d complete Monte Carlo replications** and %d method-scenario observations.\n\n",
  length(unique(figure6_raw$replication)), nrow(figure6_raw)
))
```

## Results

```{r figure6-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Prediction-squared-error experiment corresponding to Figure 6."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure6_dir, "figure6_pse_comparison.png"))
```

```{r figure6-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
figure6_display <- figure6_summary[, c(
  "rho", "method", "mean_pse", "median_pse", "q025_pse", "q975_pse"
)]
names(figure6_display) <- c(
  "rho", "Method", "Mean PSE", "Median PSE", "2.5%", "97.5%"
)
numeric_columns <- vapply(figure6_display, is.numeric, logical(1))
figure6_display[numeric_columns] <- lapply(
  figure6_display[numeric_columns], round, digits = 3
)
print(knitr::kable(figure6_display, booktabs = TRUE))
```

```{r alpha-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
alpha_counts <- as.data.frame(with(
  figure6_alpha,
  table(rho = rho, selected_alpha = selected_alpha)
))
alpha_counts <- alpha_counts[alpha_counts$Freq > 0, ]
names(alpha_counts) <- c("rho", "Selected alpha", "Frequency")
print(knitr::kable(alpha_counts, booktabs = TRUE))
```

At \(\rho=0\), the mean PSEs for Pretraining and (D_2)-only are 9.46 and
9.36, respectively. At \(\rho=0.5\), the corresponding values are 4.90 and
6.01; at \(\rho=1\), they are 6.08 and 9.14. Pretraining is therefore
comparable to the target-only fit when no coefficient component is shared and
improves as shared structure becomes available, matching the article's
qualitative conclusion.

# Reproducibility

The raw CSV files contain every Monte Carlo result rather than only the
summaries plotted above. The runner scripts checkpoint after each replication,
so rerunning them resumes rather than discards completed work. The exact
software versions are recorded in `sessionInfo.txt` within each result
directory.

To reproduce the analysis from the project root, run:

```{r run-instructions, eval=FALSE}
source(file.path(study_root, "scripts", "00_requirements.R"))
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        c(file.path(study_root, "scripts", "11_run_Figure4.R"), "--reps=100"))
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        c(file.path(study_root, "scripts", "12_run_Figure6.R"), "--reps=100"))
```
